result.question: Why follow Abimelech?

readings.support: their hearts were inclined to follow Abimelech, for they said, “He is our brother.”

readings.answer: Because he is their own flesh and blood.
readings.support: Remember that I am your own flesh and blood.

readings.answer: Because it is better for just one man to rule than seventy.
readings.support: Is it better for you that seventy men, all the sons of Jerubbaal, rule over you, or just one man?

readings.answer: Because his mother’s brothers spoke these words to the leaders.
readings.support: when his mother’s brothers spoke all these words about him in the presence of all the leaders of Shechem, their hearts were inclined to follow Abimelech

readings.answer: Because he hired men with silver to follow him.
readings.support: with which Abimelech hired some worthless and reckless men to follow him

assessments.reason: Verse 9:3 states their hearts inclined to follow Abimelech “for they said, ‘He is our brother,’” which matches the key’s reason that he was their relative.
“Own flesh and blood” (9:2) is a direct kinship claim and equivalent in meaning to being their relative.
Although Abimelech posed the one-ruler argument (9:2), the text gives the actual reason for their following as kinship: “for they said, ‘He is our brother’” (9:3).

The clause “when his mother’s brothers spoke” (9:3) sets the occasion, but the stated reason is “for they said, ‘He is our brother,’” so attributing the cause to the uncles’ speaking misreads the text’s given reason.

Verse 9:4 explicitly says Abimelech hired men to follow him with silver; if the question’s subject is those hired men, this is a valid reason, though it refers to a different group than the leaders of Shechem in 9:3.

result.reason: The question does not specify who is following Abimelech, and the passage gives different reasons for two groups: kinship for the leaders (9:3) and payment for the hired men (9:4).
